warnings: Monsoon season (Sept) – expect frequent rain, mist and possible landslides on the Kodaikanal Ghat Road; check road status before departure each day.
Boat rides on Kodaikanal Lake may be cancelled in heavy rain; use the government‑run service to avoid overcharging.
Unofficial vendors may demand extra entry fees at Bryant Park; pay only the official ₹30.
Slippery stones at Silver Cascade Falls and Pillar Rocks – wear sturdy shoes and exercise caution.

Boat‑overcharge: Unlicensed operators sometimes demand ₹500 per ride (double the official ₹150 rate). Mitigation: Use the government‑run boat service at the lake pier and verify the ₹150 rate on the notice board before boarding.

Park‑gate overcharging: Unofficial vendors may ask for ‘premium entry’ fees of ₹100–₹150 per adult at Bryant Park gate. Mitigation: Pay the official fee of ₹30 at the park office, keep the receipt, and ignore any extra charge.

Guided‑photo scam: Some ‘local guides’ offer photo‑session packages at ₹500 per picture. Mitigation: Decline the offer and use your own camera or phone; if a guide is needed, hire a certified guide from the Kodaikanal Tourist Office at ₹1500 per day.

Taxi/auto pricing inflation: Taxi from Dindigul to Kodaikanal is fixed‑rate ₹2,800–₹3,200 for a 4‑seat vehicle (meters not used); auto‑rickshaw within town charges ~₹200/km with a minimum fare of ₹100 for distances <1 km; app‑based options (Kodaikanal Cabs, Ola, Uber) are typically 10 % higher than negotiated taxi rates. Mitigation: Negotiate the taxi fare before boarding, confirm auto‑rickshaw rates, and consider app‑based services only if GPS tracking is worth the extra cost.

Landslide risk on Ghat Road during monsoon (July–early September): Mitigation: Check road conditions before departure, travel early in the day, allow extra travel time, and be prepared to use the Madurai‑Dindigul alternative if the Ghat Road is closed.

Dietary: Dominant cuisine is South Indian with liberal use of coconut oil, mustard seeds, and tamarind. Vegetarian options are abundant (≈95 % of stalls), but coconut oil may be a concern for those with coconut allergy; peanuts appear in chutneys, and pork is rare in non‑vegetarian outlets.

Medical: Nearest quality hospital is Kodaikanal Government Hospital (≈2 km from the market) with a 24‑hour emergency department, basic imaging, and a pharmacy. For serious cases, Coimbatore Medical College Hospital (~250 km) is the regional tertiary centre; air‑ambulance services may be arranged during winter peaks.
Travel checklist: Carry a personal first‑aid kit (antihistamines, motion‑sickness tablets, basic antibiotics), a reusable water bottle, and a lightweight rain jacket for sudden monsoon showers.
Transport within town: Auto‑rickshaw drivers may quote a ‘minimum fare’ of ₹100 for distances under 1 km—confirm the fare before starting.
Weather: Forecast shows light rain, overcast skies, and moderate rain likelihood; pack waterproof clothing and footwear.
Crowds: Monsoon season reduces tourist density, so expect fewer crowds at attractions, but be prepared for possible road disruptions and occasional attraction closures.

Attraction pricing (for reference): Bryant Park entry ₹30/adult, ₹15/child (3‑12 yrs), free for toddlers <3 yrs; Kodaikanal Lake entry ₹20/adult, ₹10/child (3‑12 yrs), free for toddlers; boat rides ₹150/hour (rowboat); Coaker’s Walk is free; Pillar Rocks and Silver Cascade Falls have no entry fee.
